leverage.exposure: None. The balance is positive, no offer is live, no sale is pending, and no leveraged position is open anywhere. There is nothing to unwind before the lock, which is the one risk that would outrank everything else if it existed. The single thing worth watching is tonight's market-value update: it lifts every body owned except the weakest one, which raises all five purchase budgets and is the most likely route out of the current freeze.

binding_gap: There is no formation hole this run — the shape is complete and legal. The binding constraint is capital, not shape. At exactly eleven bodies one buy permits exactly one sale, so the ceiling on any purchase is cash plus the market value of the single body it displaces, and that body must score less than the incoming man or the trade loses points. The trap is that the largest upgrade available is also the cheapest body owned: replacing the weakest man funds the smallest budget of all, while the slots with real money behind them are already filled competently. That is how a squad worth over 156 million can buy nothing.

verdict.headline: NO ACTION.
verdict.detail: NO ACTION. The squad sits at exactly eleven bodies with a positive balance, all eleven placed in the only legal formation (4-3-3), and no leveraged position open. Every worthwhile upgrade on the board costs more than the single permitted sale can raise, so the correct move before the MD3 lock is to field what is already placed and spend nothing.

sell.reason: Nothing is a recommended sale, and this is a deliberate refusal rather than an absence of candidates. With eleven bodies every sale drops the squad to ten and triggers the under-eleven penalty, which is larger than any single player's average. The conditional-sale guards carried in the ledger — replacement lands first, always — are what prevent this, and they hold. Sirch remains the designated defensive unwind lever and Conte the attacking one, but only ever after a replacement has actually landed.
